completedEvidence.what: Money representation corrected before it set
completedEvidence.detail: The policy first typed kopecks as JavaScript number. domain-core/money.ts forbids number arithmetic on money and every persisted money column in the schema is BIGINT, so the policy and its tests were moved to bigint before the convention could diverge.

completedEvidence.what: Accounting read authority proven isolating, and the proof proven able to fail
completedEvidence.detail: Six scenarios verified by hand and nine wired into the RLS integration gate: own-row read, forged organization claim, forged tenant, a dual-organization member in each direction, delegation recipient, absent context, write refusal and withheld-column refusal. Two deliberate sabotages — a policy trusting app.current_org_id alone, and an added UPDATE grant — each make the gate exit non-zero, so the checks are a regression gate rather than decoration.

The SECURITY DEFINER resolver needs pc_identity_bootstrap to retain SELECT on user_orgs. Withdrawing it was measured: the function raises permission denied, failing closed but breaking the whole read path. The migration now grants the four consulted columns itself instead of relying on the identity contour at a distance.

completedEvidence.what: Separation of duties enforced by the database, not only by policy
completedEvidence.detail: An ACTIVE signing authority must name a second approver who is neither the beneficiary nor the granter and who is a real membership of the same organization. All four violations were attempted against a live PostgreSQL 16 and refused. A revoked authority may still carry a null approver so historical rows stay writable. The command policy keys the self-approval refusal on the user rather than the membership, so one person with two memberships cannot approve their own grant by switching hats.

completedEvidence.what: Bounded write authority, with attribution enforced by the database
completedEvidence.detail: pc_accounting_command_authority may insert only rows attributing the grant to itself, and may update only status and revokedAt. Sixteen checks now run in the RLS gate. Four sabotages were used to confirm the gate can fail: a policy trusting the org setting alone, an added UPDATE grant on the read principal, full UPDATE on the command principal, and dropping the attribution condition. Capability enforcement is deliberately left in code so SQL does not become a second drifting source of truth; the database enforces attribution, scoping and immutability, which code alone cannot prove after a compromise.
